q: What temperature does water boil at in Celsius and Fahrenheit
a:
In the system of measurement commonly used today, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (°C) at standard atmospheric pressure. To convert this to Fahrenheit (°F), we use the formula:

\[ \text{°F} = \left( \text{°C} \times \frac{9}{5} \right) + 32 \]

Substituting 100°C into the formula gives:

\[ \text{°F} = \left( 100 \times \frac{9}{5} \right) + 32 = 180 + 32 = 212 \]

Therefore, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius or 212 degrees Fahrenheit under normal atmospheric conditions.
